clue.text: Set to go north of the border

definitions.meaning: a set of people, a crew or band working together

definitions.text: to go north of the border
definitions.meaning: in Scots, the dialect spoken north of the English border, the verb meaning to walk or go is spelt this way

explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, as seen from England; the Scots verb for 'go' is spelt like a word for a band of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a set of people, and in Scots dialect gang means go.

clue.text: Certainly before the right time

parts.note: yea is an old word of assent meaning yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone is sure they arrived before the proper moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a measured span of time, twelve months long.

clue.text: A frisky youngster who wrote well

definitions.meaning: a young sheep, famous for gambolling in spring fields
Charles ..., the English essayist who wrote the Essays of Elia

explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb was an English essayist of the early 1800s, best known for the Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a playful young sheep, and Lamb was a celebrated essayist.

clue.text: Pole, not on the level but stiff and pompous

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole, one of the earth's two poles
something not level is sloping or tipped over to one side

explanation.surface: A pole leaning at an angle is likened to a stuffy, pompous manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' tempts you to look for STILT, a pole you walk on; instead it is just S, for South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or writing is stiff, unnatural and pompous, as if raised up on stilts.

clue.text: Moving though quite mad proposal

parts.note: loco is Spanish-derived slang for crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for a vote

explanation.surface: A crazy proposal is nonetheless stirring someone to action.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the act or power of moving from place to place.

clue.text: The macho element that's criminal

parts.note: macho describes aggressively masculine behaviour, hence male
a factor is an element or component contributing to a result

explanation.surface: Someone claims that masculine swagger is what leads to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits crimes.

clue.text: Note this month everything is to be put back

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
inst., short for instant, is old commercial shorthand for this month
all means everything

explanation.surface: A memo announces that this month every item must be returned to its place.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) was the letter-writer's abbreviation for 'of this month', as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall something is to fit or set it up again, putting it back in position.

clue.text: The firm with little work is to shut up

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
op, short for opus, is a little word for a musical work

explanation.surface: A company short of business is going to close down.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop someone up is to confine them in a small space, like hens in a pen.

clue.text: The spiteful woman grabbing one's arm wanted the cheese

indicators.note: the spiteful woman's word takes hold of the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a cat is a catty, malicious woman
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A malicious woman seized someone's arm because she wanted cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The spiteful woman' is crossword shorthand for a catty person; 'arm' is a limb in the old sense of a body member.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft, creamy French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Famous Italian bad girl, a really bad one

indicators.note: really bad tells us these letters are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A notorious Italian woman is described as a thoroughly wicked girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'really bad' rearranges BAD, GIRL, A and I (one) into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the celebrated general who led the unification of Italy.

clue.text: When 50 follows 49 that's not good!

indicators.note: follows places the fifty after the forty-nine

parts.note: IL is a loose Roman-numeral form of 49, one before fifty
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A remark that turning fifty after forty-nine is bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 49 is XLIX in Roman numerals, but crosswords often allow IL (one before fifty).
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can mean bad or harmful, as in ill effects.

clue.text: Feeling for a pair of spectacles worn by a doctor

indicators.note: worn by means the spectacles sit on the doctor, inside his letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
OO looks like a pair of round lenses

explanation.surface: A doctor in glasses is asked how he feels.
explanation.walkthrough: The two round letters OO make a visual pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is a feeling or state of mind.

clue.text: Born in Denmark — a Dane evidently

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words a Dane evidently

explanation.surface: Someone born in Denmark must obviously be Danish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'Dane' and 'evidently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Nevertheless the head must be calm

parts.note: still can mean nevertheless, as in still, he came
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Despite everything, a leader must stay composed.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland or cape, common in British place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillness is quiet, motionless calm.

clue.text: Give voice about a holiday-maker cavorting

indicators.note: about places the singing word around the holiday-maker

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a camper is someone holidaying in a tent or van

explanation.surface: Someone sings while a holidaymaker dances about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give voice' suggests speaking up or complaining, but here it simply means to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampering is running about playfully, much like cavorting.

clue.text: Confounded triteness is of some concern

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Damned banality is a matter of some worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that interests you engages your attention and matters to you.

clue.text: A mineral prepared from fruit (sound)

parts.note: limes are green citrus fruit
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A rock seems to be made from citrus fruit, and a sound one too.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious split after the citrus fruit leaves a five-letter piece that is not a sound; move the break one letter on.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: A satellite's low point

parts.note: to low is to make the deep sound of cattle, moo
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A satellite reaches the lowest point of its orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, not a depth; N is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon is the Earth's natural satellite.

clue.text: Light diet may effect some difference

indicators.note: to effect a difference is to change something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A light diet might change things a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the diet but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytime is the part of the day when there is natural light.

clue.text: Savoury though far from well-cooked morsel

parts.note: rare meat is barely cooked, the opposite of well done
a bit is a small piece or morsel

explanation.surface: A tasty snack is described as an underdone mouthful.
explanation.walkthrough: A savoury is a small salty dish served at the end of a British meal; Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, as in Welsh rarebit, is a dish of melted cheese on toast served as a savoury.

clue.text: The odd item Edward put out

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of item are rearranged

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward threw out the strange object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ITEM into EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Emitted means given off or sent out, like light or sound.

clue.text: Dispute in the yard

definitions.meaning: to argue or box with someone
on a sailing ship a yard is a horizontal pole, one of the ship's poles

explanation.walkthrough: On a ship a yard is the pole from which a sail hangs, a kind of spar.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue, and a spar is a pole such as a ship's yard.

clue.text: It's plain the heavyweight is no egghead

parts.note: simple means plain, unadorned
a ton is a great weight

explanation.surface: Clearly the heavyweight boxer is no intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, slow-witted person, the opposite of an intellectual.

clue.text: Encourage food production

definitions.meaning: to urge someone on, as in urge on
something a hen produces that we eat

explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them, and a hen's egg is a food it produces.

clue.text: A little creature left without cash

indicators.note: without means the cash symbol is removed from the word left

parts.note: L stands for pound (libra), money

explanation.surface: A tiny animal has been abandoned penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: L, from libra, is the pound sign, hence cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small amphibian.

clue.text: Exploding star used for a branch of learning

indicators.note: an exploding thing is blown apart, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A supernova is studied as an academic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The arts are the humanities, a broad field of study.

clue.text: A man who harried Romans reformed or got shot!

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barbarian who plagued Rome either changed his ways or was shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' looks like moral improvement but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were a Germanic people who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: He'll take nothing before races — nothing

definitions.note: the definition is just 'He', a man's name; the 'll joins it to the wordplay

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
the TT, Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
O again for zero

explanation.surface: A man says he will not bother with anything before the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's given name, so it can stand for 'he'.

clue.text: A monster, and therefore elevated!

indicators.note: elevated means lifted up, so in a down entry the word reads upward

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A giant beast is said to be raised up as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.

clue.text: This arrangement could result in strikes

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word This means its letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A plan is predicted to lead to industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits are blows or strikes.

clue.text: Our responsibility?

parts.note: split in two, the word becomes a phrase saying it is we who must pay or act

explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or burden; split after the second letter it says the burden is ours.

clue.text: Choose to speak out for enfranchised people

parts.note: to elect is to choose by voting
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Voters are urged to pick and to make their voices heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of citizens entitled to vote.
